subject: Kickoff: Runtime Feature Activation (streaming + tool-calls + structured JSON outputs)
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff request - streaming + tool-calls + JSON outputs

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Priya and I ran it by the clinical informatics team and they want to move forward with a scoped rollout for two features: real-time streaming of patient summaries and a tool-call integration that hits our internal EHR lookup service. We also need structured JSON outputs (validated against a contract schema) so downstream systems can ingest results reliably.

Target: have first pilot live in a limited region by Dec 15. Main asks before we lock dates: a mutual action plan (MAP), a schema contract example we can validate against, an outline of the auth model for tool-calls, and a short checklist of operational runbooks you expect us to run.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the implementation and whether Redwood can sign off on the JSON schema compatibility test harness? Priya and I are available for a kickoff Tue/Wed next week (Nov 23/24) in the morning PST.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Product Manager, Orbital Health

--

Subject: Re: Kickoff request - streaming + tool-calls + JSON outputs

Alex — appreciate the clear ask and timeline. We’re excited to run the pilot with Orbital. I’ll own program-level coordination on Redwood's side; Camila will lead the implementation (schemas + runtime config) and Ben will manage ops/SLOs and billing alignment. Marissa will be your CS handoff for adoption.

Proposed next steps:
- Kickoff meeting: Wed Nov 24, 10:00–11:00 PST (Zoom link in the doc below)
- Deliverables before kickoff: preliminary MAP (attached), schema-matrix template, and a short ops checklist
- By Nov 30: Redwood to provide canonical JSON schema + compatibility test harness; Orbital to provide a small representative sample dataset and auth details for EHR tool endpoints

Attached: Orbit-Enablement-MAP.pdf (high-level milestones) and a link to a live MAP we can iterate on: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-orbit-map

Agenda for kickoff (30–40 min tech + 15–20 min project cadence):
1) Introductions and owner roles
2) Scope confirmation (streaming modes, tool-call patterns, structured output contract)
3) Schema expectations and test harness approach
4) Auth model for tool-calls (OAuth service account vs token exchange)
5) Milestones and success criteria
6) Open questions / risks

If that time doesn't work, let us know alternatives. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orbitalhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-22T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Implementation plan and pre-kickoff asks

Hi team — quick technical plan from the implementation side so Alex/Priya know what we'll move on after kickoff. High-level notes:

1) Schema-first approach (priority)
- I’ll populate the "schema-matrix.xlsx" with required, optional, and derived fields; we’ll version schemas semver-style and use compatibility checks in the harness.
- Deliverable: canonical schema + example payloads by Nov 30.

2) Streaming runtime (low-latency mode)
- We'll configure a dedicated streaming route and set a default kv/prefix cache for patient context to keep token cost down.
- Need: sample cadence (events/minute per patient), average expected context window (tokens), and expected concurrency.

3) Tool-calls (EHR lookup)
- We'll surface a secure tool-call connector. Two auth options: OAuth service-account (recommended) or scoped API token with IP allowlist. We’ll prepare a short integration guide for both.

4) Test harness and validation
- Redwood will run schema compatibility tests against the harness; Orbital should provide 30 representative records for full validation. If mismatches occur we’ll raise schema PRs and run regression checks.

5) Ops readiness
- I’ve attached a streaming-ops-checklist.md with rollback steps, observable SLOs to monitor, and a template incident playbook. Ben — I’ll need your input on SLO targets and alert thresholds.

Action items before kickoff:
- Alex: confirm cadence and share 30 sample records + auth contact
- Priya: confirm whether the EHR tool-call needs patient-level encryption at rest or only in transit
- Ben: propose SLO baseline (p99 latency target and error budget)
- Camila: prepare schema-matrix.xlsx and initial harness repo link

Attachments: schema-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 KB), streaming-ops-checklist.md (text, 4 KB)

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@orbitalhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-22T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Implementation plan and pre-kickoff asks

Camila / team — this is great, thanks. A few quick answers:
- Cadence: ~4–6 events per patient per hour during peak; pilot set is ~150 patients (~900 events/hour peak).
- Context window: typical patient context ~1.5k tokens, worst-case 3k.
- Concurrency: pilot expected concurrency ~10–12 requests/sec.
- Encryption: patient identifiers must be encrypted at rest (HIPAA controls); token-in-transit is fine for tool-calls, but we’ll provide an encrypted service account key if needed.

I attached a small representative sample and the JSON contract we’re starting from (orbital_sample_schema.json). We can do kickoff Wed 11/24 at 10:00 PST — confirmed on our side.

One question: for the test harness, will you publish a simple compatibility report (pass/fail + diff) that we can automatically ingest into our CI? That would be ideal.

Thanks — see you Wednesday.
Alex

--

Alex / Priya — quick confirmation from ops and next steps so everyone has expectations before kickoff:

Deliverables and owners:
- Redwood: canonical JSON schema + compatibility harness (Camila) — due Nov 30
- Orbital: 30 sample records + auth contact (Alex) — due Nov 24 end of day
- Ops SLO proposal (Ben) — draft by Nov 26; target p99 latency: 350ms for streaming token responses, error budget 0.5%
- MAP updates and weekly cadence: Marissa to run weekly status syncs; first 2-week checkpoint Dec 8

- Camila/Ben will set up a staging environment and a canary route for the tool-call connector; we’ll run a smoke test with your sample data before enabling production traffic.
- For schema compatibility reports: yes, we’ll publish a machine-readable pass/fail JSON + unified diff to the linked MAP doc (and provide a webhook to your CI).

Next meeting: Kickoff Wed 2027-11-24 10:00 PST — Zoom invite sent in calendar.

If anything changes on the Orbital side please flag prior to kickoff. Looking forward to a smooth rollout.

Ben Carter
